description: This course covers the principles of securing IT infrastructure, including network security protocols such as TLS 1.3, IPSec, and SSH; cryptographic algorithms like AES, RSA, and ECC; and security frameworks such as NIST SP 800-53 and ISO/IEC 27001. Topics include secure configuration of firewalls, intrusion detection systems (IDS), and virtual private networks (VPNs); secure storage and transmission of data using PKI and digital certificates; and the use of tools like Wireshark, Nmap, and Metasploit for vulnerability assessment and penetration testing. The course also explores secure cloud infrastructure, including AWS and Azure security best practices, and the implementation of secure access controls using LDAP, RADIUS, and Diameter protocols. Students will analyze real-world security breaches and design secure infrastructure architectures.

clos.text: Define cryptographic algorithms such as AES, RSA, and ECC and their roles in securing data transmission and storage.
Describe the architecture and functionality of firewalls, intrusion detection systems, and virtual private networks.
Explain the principles of secure configuration and management of network devices using industry standards like NIST SP 800-53.
Apply security tools such as Wireshark, Nmap, and Metasploit to conduct vulnerability assessments and penetration testing.
Design a secure infrastructure architecture that incorporates PKI, secure access controls, and cloud security best practices.
